summary: Session 4 of 4, the set-terminal session: a bounded Windows OS-capture pilot against this repository's own product, ending in a measurement. THE CRITERIA WERE MADE CHECKABLE, NOT JUST WRITTEN DOWN. The spec says criteria decided after the first capture are not criteria, so they were committed as a machine-readable file BEFORE any capture, the harness reads that file, refuses to run without it, and stamps its SHA-256 into every measurement it writes; the verdict is then computed from it by a separate pure module that contains no threshold of its own. Anyone can recompute the verdict from the committed numbers and the committed thresholds with --evaluate-only. Seven criteria, each with an instrument, and a CONTROL wherever the claim would otherwise be unfalsifiable -- a correlation threshold with no decoy cannot tell a working instrument from one that returns 1.0 for everything, and a leakage scan with nothing to find passes whether or not the detector works. The criteria were amended ONCE, before the first capture and with the amendment journaled, after probing found the operator's default OBS scene collection carries a live webcam, a microphone and Desktop Audio. The harness always builds its own scene collection so none of that was ever going to be in frame -- but an unasserted safety property is a hope, and this one is the operator's camera. WHAT THE PILOT ESTABLISHES. Windows Graphics Capture through OBS records the AI Work Explorer cleanly and repeatably: correlation 0.9996 against a Playwright screenshot of the same window on every capture, against a decoy that scored 0.2978; zero occluder pixels in frame with an occluder covering 80.8% of the target and holding foreground focus; frame dimensions exactly equal to the window's physical pixels, and following a deliberate resize; anchor uncertainty around 110ms against a 1500ms bar; deterministic cleanup across every attempt including three induced part-way failures. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated rather than left to be assumed. One display scale (100%) was exercised -- changing the operator's live scaling would disrupt the desktop they work on, so a window-resize variant covers the same dimension-blindness failure mode and the gap is recorded. And C1 measures OBS's capture SOURCE, not the encoded file: a capture that was perfect at the source and black in the file would pass it. The file is corroborated only by its size and by a human watching it. FOUR DEFECTS FOUND BY PROBING RATHER THAN BY REASONING, before the measurement ran: --websocket_port is honoured and does not ENABLE the server; a leftover .sentinel marker raises a modal crash dialog that HANGS the next launch rather than failing it; RecQuality=Small makes OBS accept StartRecord and never start the output, with no websocket error and no line in OBS's own log; and cleanup PREDICTED OBS's filenames instead of observing them, so it deleted nothing and reported success -- the worst of both. Two settings were removed rather than a workaround added. THE CRITERIA CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN THE PRODUCT, which is the whole point of writing them first. The last caption cue ended 32-83ms AFTER the recording did, on every one of the first eleven captures. Nothing else in the session would have found it -- the videos look fine and the captions look fine, and the two were only ever compared because a criterion said to. Fixed by holding the recording 750ms past the last step, which also replaces a hard cut on the frame of the final click with a beat the viewer can read the result in, and re-measured across a full second round of captures rather than asserted. THREE CRITERIA ARE REPORTED UNMET, and they are three different kinds of thing. C4 was a real defect and is fixed. C2's substantive claim passes absolutely (zero leakage) while its detector CONTROL came in at 0.44 against a 0.50 bar, because the occluder doubles as C1's structured decoy and the captured window includes browser chrome -- deliberately NOT retuned, since adjusting the instrument to pass is the same sin as moving the threshold. C7's no-audio-track clause cannot be satisfied through OBS configuration at all: four configurations were tried and OBS muxes a track regardless, though no audio SOURCE exists, so the track can only carry silence. THE RECORDER SHIPS PROVISIONALLY, and this session does not self-authorize that. Adjudicating a criterion as non-blocking reduces verification, which is inside the decision-rights hard carve-out, so whether a provably silent audio track is acceptable is put to the operator as item A of the guided look rather than settled here. What the spec's own bar asked for -- ten consecutive clean captures from a fresh fixture, no wrong-window capture, no privacy leakage -- was met. What the machine verdict says is FAIL, because this session set itself extra clauses and two did not come out. Both statements are true and the record keeps both. A METHODOLOGICAL FLAW WAS CAUGHT IN THE HARNESS ITSELF: the run carrying the controls repoints the live capture at the decoy part way through, so its VIDEO is not a recording of the walkthrough even though its measurements are sound. It is excluded from the ten in CODE -- derived from the record rather than trusted to a flag -- and a supplementary run supplies the tenth clean capture. VERIFICATION RAN FOUR ROUNDS AND FOUND SEVEN DISTINCT DEFECTS, every one accepted and none disputed. The most serious: capture failures DESTROYED the walkthrough instead of degrading -- only ObsUnavailableError was caught, so the ambiguity refusal (a plain Error, hit routinely by a developer with a second Extension Development Host open) deleted the run directory and exited non-zero, leaving someone who wanted a walkthrough and could not have a video with NEITHER. Two more were defects in the instruments built to prevent false positives: C6 passed on the dependency-absent variants while asserting in its own note that those were the part-way failures it asked for (they die during setup, two before a scene collection exists), and supplementary runs counted toward the ten-clean-run bar without being evaluated against C1-C4 -- so on the designed path the one recording that supplies the tenth capture was the one recording nobody checked. THE GATE TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS AND VERIFICATION REJECTED THE FIRST TWO: 'provisional' in an outcome document ('calling it provisional in prose does not enforce a gate'), then a notice that printed the FAIL verdict and recorded anyway ('leaves the operator's decision right advisory rather than enforced'). The CLI now fails closed, reads its approval from the committed record, and names the two routes that would unlock it -- neither available to a session on its own authority. THE FFMPEG FALLBACK IS MEASURED, on operator direction after the documented-not-done version was rejected: gdigrab produced a UNIFORMLY BLACK FRAME on the Electron window (every pixel 0,0,0; eight seconds at 16 KB against ~37 MB for a comparable OBS capture) while carrying a video stream and no audio track. It satisfies the one clause OBS structurally cannot and fails the one that matters most, confirming the operator's 2026-08-15 ruling rather than overturning it. That black frame read as a failure only because a falsifier written before the measurement existed makes a zero-variance frame score 0 rather than 1. SUITES: pytest 4986 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed, mocha 1548 passed, Layer 3 37 passed, all green and all recorded after the last code change. ONE ITEM IS OPEN AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S: the gate fix landed after the loop reached its bound of two remediation-review cycles, so it is remediated but unverified, and only an operator-authorized round can confirm it. CLOSED ON A VERIFIED ROUND THE OPERATOR AUTHORIZED. The gate fix landed after the bounded loop was spent, so the operator authorized exactly one more cycle rather than the session self-authorizing it; round 5 returned VERIFIED with 0 findings and 0 fix verdicts rejected. THE SET IS NOW SIX SESSIONS, NOT FOUR, on operator direction taken as this session closed: Session 5 measures whether the capture dependencies can be isolated in a container -- with the operator's own correction to this session's framing, that the answer is to put BOTH VS Code and OBS inside rather than to capture a host window from outside -- and Session 6 diagnoses why the advisory path-aware critique could not reach two providers. Session 6 is now the set-terminal session and inherits change-log.md and the Step 9 review, both of which this session wrote early and which will be refreshed there.

residuals.summary: THE ADVISORY PATH-AWARE CRITIQUE COULD NOT REACH TWO PROVIDERS ON THIS SEAT, so no path-aware-critique.json was produced. Three attempts, google succeeding every time and openai failing every time, in two distinct ways: (1) the default openai critic raised DeterministicServantViolation -- 'grep: tool result does not match raw ground truth' -- which is the servant-integrity guard correctly refusing a critic that paraphrased tool output rather than reporting its bytes; (2) openai pinned to gpt-5-6-sol and then to gpt-5-5 both returned HTTP 400 from https://api.openai.com/v1/responses. The second is the sharper signal: the SAME openai models answered five session-verification calls in this session without trouble, so the ordinary routed path works while the pull-critique path (tool-using, Responses API) does not. That is a router-side defect worth its own look, not a provider outage. The gate is ADVISORY and does not block the close; the documented manual flow (two clean-context passes in a Copilot editor) remains available. Not worked around by using anthropic as the second critic: anthropic is this orchestrator's own provider, and manufacturing a passing artifact from a same-provider second opinion would satisfy the letter of '>= 2 distinct providers' while defeating the independence it exists for.
residuals.owner: a follow-on look at the pull-critique openai transport

reason.specifics: Session 5 is the containerised-capture measurement, and it is this session's discipline applied somewhere else: fix the criteria before the first container run, reuse s4-pilot-criteria where the claims are identical, and say plainly which criteria a container cannot be asked to meet. The operator supplied the shape -- VS Code and OBS inside the same container, capturing a display that never leaves it -- which is feasible on a Linux guest and corrects this session's framing that a container cannot capture a host window. The real cost is fidelity, not feasibility: Podman on Windows is a Linux VM, so what gets recorded is Linux VS Code rather than the Windows VS Code staff run, and that trade has to be named rather than discovered. MEASURE THE CHEAP MITIGATION FIRST: OBS's own --only-bundled-plugins flag may buy most of the risk reduction for none of the complexity, and this session observed the operator's install loading a DeckLink SDK, an NVIDIA filters plugin, a CEF browser source and an ML background-removal model, none of which this framework wants. ai_router/podman_sandbox.py (Set 069 S4) already implements the container-as-trust-boundary principle and is the thing to build on.

next_orchestrator.first_action: Measure the OBS plugin surface with and without --only-bundled-plugins BEFORE building any container. If the flag buys most of the risk reduction, the container may not be worth its cost -- and that is a real answer, arrived at cheaply.
